question:
This is a secret message my friend gave me. It says where we should meet for our picnic on Friday. The only problem is, it’s encrypted in the Caesar cipher, so I can’t read it. Can you tell me what it says? This is the message:

Zsmxsm sc sx Zyvilsec Zvkjk.

history.name: AlgorithmDesign_Expert
history.content: Plan: We can solve this quickly without writing code by exploiting common Caesar patterns. The repeated short words "sc sx" likely map to "is in" under some shift. I'll ask NaturalLanguageProcessing_Expert to do a fast mental decode using that anchor and confirm the full sentence.

history.name: NaturalLanguageProcessing_Expert
history.content:
Using the anchor: if "sc" -> "is", then s->i is a shift of 10 backward (s to i), and c->s also fits shift 10. Apply shift 10 to the whole text:
- Z -> P
- s -> i
- m -> c
- x -> n
- s -> i
- m -> c
So "Zsmxsm" -> "Picnic".
For the phrase:
- "sc" -> "is"
- "sx" -> "in"
For "Zyvilsec" with shift 10 gives "Polybius" (Z->P, y->o, v->l, i->y, l->b, s->i, e->u, c->s). And "Zvkjk" -> "Plaza".
Thus the decrypted message reads: "Picnic is in Polybius Plaza." Since "Polybius" is the standard name (also the famous cipher term), I'll stick with that spelling.

history.content: Final decrypted message: Picnic is in Polybius Plaza.
